raw_findings.body: Introduces an unrelated git submodule pointing to an external commit unrelated to the error-upsampling feature; checkouts can produce an empty/broken 'sentry-repo' directory or fail submodule initialization, and it pollutes repo metadata unrelated to this PR's scope
raw_findings.failure_mode: Checkout/build pipelines may fail or produce an inconsistent working tree when the submodule reference cannot be resolved
raw_findings.impact: Introduces an unrelated git submodule pointing to an external commit unrelated to the error-upsampling feature; checkouts can produce an empty/broken 'sentry-repo' directory or fail submodule initialization, and it pollutes repo metadata unrelated to this PR's scope
raw_findings.root_cause: A gitlink/submodule entry for 'sentry-repo' was committed as part of this PR, unrelated to the intended change set
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the accidentally-added 'sentry-repo' submodule gitlink entry from this patch before merging
raw_findings.title: Accidental git submodule 'sentry-repo' added by this patch
raw_findings.trigger: Anyone clones/updates the repository or CI runs a submodule-aware checkout after this patch is merged

raw_findings.body: The substring check returns True for queries that explicitly exclude error events or reference an unrelated value, causing the sum(sample_weight)-based upsampling transform to be incorrectly applied to non-error/transaction data, producing wrong aggregate counts or a Snuba error when sample_weight does not exist for those events
raw_findings.failure_mode: Incorrect column transformation applied to queries that are not truly error-focused, yielding wrong statistics or backend errors
raw_findings.impact: The substring check returns True for queries that explicitly exclude error events or reference an unrelated value, causing the sum(sample_weight)-based upsampling transform to be incorrectly applied to non-error/transaction data, producing wrong aggregate counts or a Snuba error when sample_weight does not exist for those events
raw_findings.root_cause: Error-focus detection relies on naive substring containment on the raw query string instead of exact filter parsing
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a proper filter/token-aware check (or the existing search parser) instead of a raw substring match, and explicitly exclude negated matches like '!event.type:error'
raw_findings.title: _is_error_focused_query mis-detects negated/related event.type filters as error-focused
raw_findings.trigger: A discover query with query string like '!event.type:error' (explicitly excluding errors) or a tag value such as 'event.type:error_custom' is submitted against the discover dataset

raw_findings.body: Clients can invoke the internal aggregation directly on projects/events lacking a sample_weight column, returning misleading counts or triggering a Snuba query error, circumventing the intended allowlist-based gating
raw_findings.evidence:
SnQLFunction(
                    "upsampled_count",
                    required_args=[],
                    # Optimized aggregation for error upsampling - assumes sample_weight
                    # exists for all events in allowlisted projects as per schema design
                    snql_aggregate=lambda args, alias: Function(
                        "toInt64",
                        [Function("sum", [Column("sample_weight")])],
                        alias,
                    ),
                    default_result_type="number",
                ),
raw_findings.failure_mode: Bypasses the allowlist-based eligibility gate, exposing an internal-only aggregation to arbitrary API callers
raw_findings.impact: Clients can invoke the internal aggregation directly on projects/events lacking a sample_weight column, returning misleading counts or triggering a Snuba query error, circumventing the intended allowlist-based gating
raw_findings.root_cause: The 'upsampled_count' function was registered in the public function_converter map without the private flag used by other internal-only aggregate functions
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Mark the new SnQLFunction with private=True (as done for the existing column_hash function) so it is only resolvable via internal code paths that already validate eligibility
raw_findings.title: New 'upsampled_count' SnQL function is not marked private, bypassing allowlist gating
raw_findings.trigger: A client issues a discover-dataset query directly requesting field/yAxis=upsampled_count() for a project not in the client_error_sampling allowlist, bypassing the eligibility check that only exists in organization_events_stats.py

raw_findings.body: The function has no call sites anywhere in the patch or referenced code paths, so the documented cache-invalidation contract is never fulfilled; stale eligibility results can persist for up to 60 seconds with no mechanism to force a refresh
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unreachable code that contradicts its own documented behavior, misleading maintainers into believing invalidation is handled automatically
raw_findings.impact: The function has no call sites anywhere in the patch or referenced code paths, so the documented cache-invalidation contract is never fulfilled; stale eligibility results can persist for up to 60 seconds with no mechanism to force a refresh
raw_findings.root_cause: A cache-invalidation helper was added without integrating it into any option-change code path
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Wire invalidate_upsampling_cache into the option-change handler/signal for 'issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist', or remove the unused function/misleading docstring if invalidation isn't actually needed
raw_findings.title: invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code, contradicting its own cache-invalidation contract
raw_findings.trigger: An operator updates 'issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist' expecting the documented invalidation ('This should be called when the allowlist configuration changes') to take effect

raw_findings.body: Errors such as AttributeError (when contexts is None) or ValueError (non-numeric client_sample_rate) are silently discarded, so sample_rate is silently omitted and the test proceeds with unexpected data instead of failing loudly, masking real fixture bugs
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test helper silently ignores malformed input, producing misleading test results or hard-to-diagnose downstream failures
raw_findings.impact: Errors such as AttributeError (when contexts is None) or ValueError (non-numeric client_sample_rate) are silently discarded, so sample_rate is silently omitted and the test proceeds with unexpected data instead of failing loudly, masking real fixture bugs

finding.verifier_reason: The code at lines 347-357 uses defensive exception handling in a test utility. The `.get()` chain on lines 348-350 cannot raise AttributeError since `get()` returns `{}` as default. The broad `except Exception: pass` is a code style issue, not a bug - the function is designed to silently skip invalid data in test fixtures, which is intentional behavior for test helpers.
